data.one_liner: Generate and verify TOTP and HOTP one-time passwords for 2FA and MFA.
data.what_it_does: Generates and verifies time-based (TOTP) and counter-based (HOTP) one-time passwords adhering to RFC 6238 and RFC 4226. Supports parsing and generating Google Authenticator otpauth:// URIs, drift tolerance, and secure Base32 secret generation.
use_when: You need to implement two-factor or multi-factor authentication in a Dart or Flutter application.
You need to generate or parse Google Authenticator otpauth:// URIs for QR codes.
avoid_when: You require client-side storage or server-side counter persistence out of the box without building it yourself.
strengths: RFC test-vector validated against RFC 4226 and RFC 6238 reference vectors.
Constant-time verification to prevent timing attacks.
Pure Dart with zero Flutter dependencies, supporting multiple algorithms (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512).
weaknesses: Requires manual implementation of server-side counter persistence and secret management.
On the web, integers are exact only up to 2^53, so extremely large HOTP counters require a native-int target.
